info.title: BricketX Portal API — Investor
info.description: Slice 1 (Identity & Onboarding): auth, KYC/KYB onboarding, document upload, and admin compliance review. Slice 2 (Catalog, in progress): category + package admin CRUD and allocations (content/media/publish and investor-facing read routes are a later pass). Generated from the same zod schemas the routes validate against — see src/openapi/document.ts.

post.summary: A1 — Register a new investor
post.description: Answers identically whether or not the address already has an account, so it cannot be used to find out who is registered: a new address gets an account and an emailed 6-digit code; an existing one gets an email saying so (or, if that account never finished verifying, a fresh code). The email is trimmed and lower-cased. The response carries no user id - verify-email and resend-otp are keyed by the email.

201.description: Accepted. A code (or an "already registered" notice) is on its way to the address.

email.description: The address as stored (trimmed, lower-case) — use it for verify-email and resend-otp.

429.description: Too many attempts (rate limit or account lock). A Retry-After header says how long to wait.

post.summary: A2 — Verify the email OTP
post.description: Body is { email, otp } (it was { userId, otp }).

400.description: Code invalid or expired (also returned for an address with no account)

429.description: Five wrong guesses used this code up (exact, even for simultaneous requests), or the address's rate limit tripped. A new code is not issued until the old one would have expired.

post.summary: A3 — Resend the email OTP
post.description: Body is { email } (it was { userId }). The same 200 for any address; at most one per cooldown period per address. A resend keeps the live code's attempt count.

429.description: Resend cooldown still active, or the rate limit tripped

post.summary: A4 — Login

200.description: Either tokens (an investor or an agent — never asked for a code, even an agent who set up two-factor sign-in before agents stopped using it), mfaRequired:true plus a single-use mfaToken (an admin role with TOTP enrolled — call A4b next with that token), or mfaEnrollmentRequired:true (any admin role — admin, finance_admin, compliance_admin or super_admin — that has not enrolled TOTP, since two-factor sign-in is mandatory for every admin: the accessToken returned is restricted to POST /auth/mfa/enroll/start and /confirm — every other endpoint refuses it — and no refresh cookie is set; enroll, then sign in again). Sets `refreshToken` as an httpOnly cookie when tokens are returned.

mfaToken.description: Single-use, 5 minutes, bound to this sign-in. Send it with the TOTP code to POST /auth/mfa/verify.

403.description: Account suspended

429.description: Too many attempts (rate limit or account lock). A Retry-After header says how long to wait.

post.summary: A4b — Verify admin TOTP and receive tokens
post.description: Body is { mfaToken, totp } or { mfaToken, recoveryCode } - exactly one of totp / recoveryCode. mfaToken is the single-use value A4 returned: bound to that sign-in, valid 5 minutes, dead after success or 5 attempts. A code works once per account per 30-second step. A recovery code (XXXXX-XXXXX, from enrolment or regeneration) works once, in place of an authenticator code; when one is used the response also says how many remain, and the admin and the super admin are emailed. Wrong codes of either kind also count toward the account lockout.

200.description: MFA verified, tokens issued. Sets `refreshToken` as an httpOnly cookie.

recoveryCodesRemaining.description: Present only when a recovery code was used: how many unused ones the admin has left. Warn them when it is low and offer POST /auth/mfa/recovery-codes/regenerate.

400.description: MFA not configured for this account

401.description: The token is unknown, expired or used up, or the code is wrong or was already used

429.description: Too many wrong codes for this sign-in, the account is locked, or the rate limit tripped - sign in again later

post.summary: A5 — Rotate the refresh token

200.description: Refresh rotated (old token spent). Sets a new `refreshToken` cookie. Presenting the SAME token again within 30 seconds (a double reload, two tabs) returns the same new session: the same new cookie value, an access token with the same expiry, and the cookie's remaining life - nothing is extended. After 30 seconds a spent token ends the whole session family.

401.description: Missing, revoked, or expired refresh token

403.description: The request names a site (Origin/Referer) that is not an allowed origin

429.description: Too many attempts (rate limit or account lock). A Retry-After header says how long to wait.

post.summary: A6 — Logout
post.description: Needs no access token - only the refresh cookie - so a person whose access token has expired can still end their session. Always 204 (an unknown cookie is simply nothing to revoke).

403.description: The request names a site (Origin/Referer) that is not an allowed origin

429.description: Too many attempts (rate limit or account lock). A Retry-After header says how long to wait.

post.summary: A7 — Request a password reset code
post.description: Emails a 6-digit OTP code (not a link/token) — same UX pattern as A2 email verification. Redesigned post-spec from the original opaque-token flow.

200.description: Generic success — does not reveal whether the email is registered

429.description: One request a minute and three an hour per address (whether or not it has an account). While a code is live its attempt count carries over; once used up no new code goes out until it expires.

post.summary: A8 — Reset password using the emailed OTP code
post.description: Every failure (no such flow, wrong code, too many attempts, expired) returns the same generic error — never distinguishes "no account" from "wrong code", preserving A7's non-enumeration property. Revokes every refresh token for the account (all sessions; A9 change-password instead hands the caller's own session a new pair).

200.description: Password reset, all refresh tokens revoked

429.description: Too many attempts (rate limit or account lock). A Retry-After header says how long to wait.

post.summary: A9 — Change password while logged in
post.description: Distinct from A7/A8's logged-out forgot/reset flow. Ends every session of the account at once (earlier access tokens stop working on admin routes, every refresh token is revoked). If this browser's refresh cookie came with the request, this session is handed a new pair: `accessToken` in the body and a new refresh cookie; otherwise (the investor app) every session ends. A wrong currentPassword counts toward the account lockout.

200.description: Password changed, every other session ended

accessToken.description: Present when the request carried this browser's refresh cookie: a new access token for this session (a new refresh cookie is set too). Every other session, and every earlier access token, has ended.

401.description: Missing/invalid access token, or currentPassword is incorrect

429.description: Too many attempts (rate limit or account lock). A Retry-After header says how long to wait.

get.summary: A10 — Get the caller's own identity
get.description: Post-spec addition: neither the MFA-verify response nor the refresh response ever carried user identity (both return only accessToken), so a page reload or any MFA-gated login (mandatory for admin-web) left the frontend with no user data. fullName is set at registration (A1) and is null for admin-only accounts with no investor_profile. investorRfid is the investor's own RFID (BX-RFID-xxxxxx), generated once at their first activation and never changed; null before that and for admin accounts.

investorRfid.description: The investor's RFID (BX-RFID-xxxxxx), generated once at their first activation and never changed; null until then, and for accounts with no investor profile.

get.summary: Get the caller's own agreement-profile data (identity doc, next of kin, bank details)
get.description: Identity document number is the investor's own record only — never returned for any other investor. `investingAccount` is the payout bank account, MASKED (the account number or IBAN shows only its last four characters). `requirements` says which details the agreement requires of THIS investor (`required`) and which are still missing (`missing`, each with a message written for the investor) — use it for required markers and a checklist instead of keeping a list of your own; the bank-account items follow the bank's country (see GET /investors/me/bank-account/requirements). `pendingBankChange` is a bank-details change waiting for its emailed code, if any. The account's currency is always USD.

200.description: Current values — null where nothing has been saved yet

identityDocumentNumber.description: The investor's own record only, masked to its last four characters (••••1234) - the whole number is never returned here. To change it, send the new number in a PATCH.

investingAccount.description: The payout bank account, masked: the account number or IBAN shows only its last four characters.

pendingBankChange.description: A bank-details change waiting for the investor's emailed code, if any. Signing is refused (409) while one is waiting.

bankAccountChange.description: Only on PATCH: what happened to the bank-account parts of the request (applied at once when no bank details existed yet; waiting for the emailed code when it changes existing ones; or unchanged). Null when none were sent. Everything else in the request applied at once.

patch.summary: Update the caller's own agreement-profile data
patch.description: Every field is independently optional. The identity document and next of kin apply at once (omitted = untouched, explicit null = cleared). The payout bank account — accountHolder (an individual's first and last name; a company's name is its registered name), accountAddress (structured) and bankDetails — each present part replaces the stored one. A save with a required bank detail empty (bank country, bank name, holder first and last name, account number or IBAN, SWIFT/BIC) is 422 BANK_DETAILS_INVALID with details.fieldErrors per field, nothing saved; no value is checked for its format. Details that do not exist yet (no account, or none with bank details) apply AT ONCE with no code (`bankAccountChange.status` applied, with the saved account); a CHANGE to existing details applies only when the investor confirms the 6-digit code emailed to them (pending_confirmation, POST /investors/me/bank-account/changes/{changeId}/confirm); identical details are `unchanged` and do nothing. Airwallex's check runs in the background, never blocks a save and is not shown to the investor (admins see its result). `legalName` is refused with 422 — the account holder is entered as accountHolder. `bankDetails.currency` is refused with 422 — every payout is USD. Editing these never changes a past investment's own frozen snapshot (investments.agreementPartySnapshot) — only what a FUTURE investment would pre-fill from. Signing is refused (409) while a bank change to existing details is waiting for its code.

legalName.description: Refused — send nothing here. The account holder is entered as a first and last name (accountHolder), not a single legal name.

currency.description: Refused — send nothing here. Currency can't be chosen — all investments and payouts are in US dollars.

post.summary: 6.3 — Commit to a published package (creates a draft investment)
post.description: Idempotent per (investor, package) while the existing one stays in draft: calling this again for a package the caller already has an unsigned draft investment in returns that same draft (200) instead of creating a second one — this is how the invest flow resumes after the investor abandons it partway through. The submitted body is ignored on a resume; use PATCH /investments/:id to change an existing draft's fields. A brand-new draft is 201. Every validation failure names the specific field/reason — see the 422/403/404/409 responses below.

get.summary: 6.5 — Get BricketX's bank details and this investment's payment reference
get.description: Only available once the investment has been signed (docs_signed or later) — a draft investment 409s, since there's nothing to fund yet. The first read after signing moves the investment from docs_signed to pending_funding; later reads (including once funds have actually arrived) are a no-op. The reference must be included with the wire transfer so it can be matched automatically; bank charges along the way may mean a slightly smaller amount is received than was sent.

200.description: Bank details, the payment reference, and factual notes about the transfer

schema.description: notes[0] states the reference must be included with the transfer; notes[1] states bank charges may reduce the amount received, worded factually since management hasn't decided how a shortfall is treated.

post.summary: Cancel your own draft investment
post.description: No request body. Cancels an investment that is still a draft: not signed, no payment declared or received, no deposit tied to it, not in a pool and not a reinvestment. The investment is kept with status cancelled (it is never deleted) and leaves the investor free to start again on the same package. No money has moved, so nothing is booked and nobody is notified. Cancelling again returns 200 with the same investment. Any other state 409s with error.code INVESTMENT_NOT_CANCELLABLE and a message written for the investor (signed, a reinvestment, in a pool, a payment on record, or cancelled some other way, for example by a refund).

post.summary: Tell BricketX you have sent your payment
post.description: No request body. INFORMATION ONLY — records that the investor says they have sent their transfer, and when (investment.paymentSentAt), and emails the finance/admin team so they know one is on its way. It posts nothing to the ledger, moves no money and does not change the investment's status; the payment only counts once it actually arrives (bank deposit matched automatically or by an admin). Allowed while status is pending_funding (with the payment instructions shown) or funding_shortfall (the investor sends the difference); a draft/docs_signed investment, or one whose funds are all in, 409s. In pending_funding it records paymentSentAt; in funding_shortfall it records topUpSentAt instead, leaving the original paymentSentAt as history, and emails admins again because a top-up is new information. Declaring again in the same stage is harmless: it returns 200 with the ORIGINAL time and notifies nobody again. There is no undo. Returns the investment, so the UI can read paymentSentAt straight off the response.

get.summary: Download the payment instructions as a PDF
get.description: A one-page document titled "Payment Instructions" (deliberately not an invoice) with BricketX's letterhead, the investor's name (the company name for a business investor), the package, the amount, the payment reference and the bank details frozen to this investment — the same account GET .../funding-instructions shows, never the current one — plus the note that bank charges may reduce the amount received. Generated fresh on every call, never stored. Bearer auth is required, so a plain link or window.open will not work: fetch it as a blob with the Authorization header and save it (Content-Disposition suggests the filename). Same availability as funding-instructions: a draft investment 409s, and the first call after signing moves docs_signed to pending_funding exactly like that endpoint does.

post.summary: Sign the agreement — the core e-sign operation
post.description: One flat `values[]` array covers every field kind: a signer_entered field submits `value`, a signature/initials field submits `signature` ({method:"drawn",objectKey} from the presign endpoint above, or {method:"typed",text}). Who signs besides the investor is `presentRoles`: the keys of the envelope's `signers[]` signing now, in person on this device after the investor (every one with required:true must be listed). A signer left out is skipped entirely: their boxes are left blank on the document, whatever their required flag, and no recipient is made for them. `witnessPresent` is deprecated (true = presentRoles ["witness"]) and still accepted until every app has switched. Each signer present gets their own recipient row (their typed name as displayName, their typed email if their boxes ask for one; no account, never emailed). A typed box is checked by its `format`: email and phone by the registration rules (a phone's spaces, brackets, dashes and dots are ignored), a name box in Latin letters (422 NAME_NOT_LATIN, details.fieldId). A required field (auto with no data, or signer_entered/signature not submitted) refuses signing with 422 `details.missing` — nothing is generated or persisted. On success: the final PDF is stamped, hashed, stored privately; both signers' audit rows (ip, user agent, document hash, display name) are written; investments.agreement_party_snapshot is frozen from CURRENT data (not from commit time); the investment moves to docs_signed. Refused (409) if the envelope isn't pending (already signed) or the investment has left draft. Refused (422, code UNSUPPORTED_CHARACTERS) if any text going onto the agreement — the investor's name, address, bank account holder, a typed signature, a witness name — uses characters the document can't print (Arabic, Urdu and other non-Latin scripts; Latin letters like ş or ł are fine): nothing is signed, stored or hashed, so a corrected profile, or a drawn instead of typed signature, can be submitted on the same envelope.

Every signer with required: true must be listed (else 422 ROLE_REQUIRED); a key that isn't one of this agreement's signers is 422 ROLE_UNKNOWN. A signer left out is skipped: their boxes are ignored and nothing is recorded for them.

witnessPresent.description: Deprecated: send presentRoles instead. true means presentRoles ["witness"], false or left out means none. Sent together with presentRoles, the two must agree about the witness (else 422 PRESENT_ROLES_CONFLICT). true on an agreement with no witness: 400.

Nothing in this response says whether the bank network has accepted the details: that check runs in the background and only admins see its answer. `detailsChangedAt` is when the details last changed (null when it was not recorded). `pendingChange` is a change waiting for its emailed code.

get.summary: The fields the bank-details form needs for a bank in a chosen country
get.description: The same list for every country, kept by BricketX (nothing is asked of Airwallex): render the form from `fields` — each has the request-body path to send it in (`name`), a label for the investor and whether it is required. Required: the bank's country and name, a SWIFT/BIC, an account number or an IBAN (`oneOf`: neither is required on its own, one of the two is) and, for an individual, the account holder's first and last name (a company's holder is its registered name). The holder's address is optional. No field has a format rule: a save is refused only for an empty required field.

post.summary: Submit a payout bank account — first entry applies at once, a change to existing details needs the emailed code
post.description: Send accountHolder, accountAddress and/or bankDetails (each present part replaces the stored one). BricketX checks that every required detail of the whole result is given: bank country, bank name, the holder's first and last name (an individual), an account number or an IBAN, and a SWIFT/BIC; the holder's address is optional. A save with anything required empty is refused with 422 BANK_DETAILS_INVALID — details.fieldErrors holds the request-body path of EACH empty required field -> its messages, so a form can mark every one at once, and details.issues carries the same findings as field, label, kind, message. Nothing is saved. No value is checked for its format; the IBAN and account number are stored trimmed, upper-cased and without spaces. Airwallex checks the details too, in the background, but NEVER blocks the save and nothing it says is in any investor response (admins see the result). Details that do not exist yet (no account, or none with bank details) apply AT ONCE with no code: 200, status `applied`, with the saved `bankAccount` and `readiness`, and the investor is emailed. A CHANGE to existing details sends a 6-digit code and returns 202 `pending_confirmation` with the pending change; it applies only on confirm; a new submission replaces an earlier pending change, and the investor can withdraw it with POST /investors/me/bank-account/changes/{changeId}/cancel. 200 with status `unchanged` when nothing differs from what is saved: no pending change, no code, no history, no email. At most 5 submissions per investor per hour (429). Refunds and payouts go only to details Airwallex has accepted; otherwise they are held and an admin follows up.

post.summary: Start the new investment from the terms we agreed
post.description: Allowed once an administrator has confirmed the terms of your reinvestment (`request.plan`). Creates the new investment as a draft with the amount, package, term and payout schedule fixed (they cannot be changed afterwards), recording your acceptance of the package's disclaimer and the professional investor declaration. Then continue exactly as for any investment: confirm your details and sign the new agreement. There is no payment to make: it is funded from your matured principal.
